newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oman stocks tick lower in active week's trade.
newsitem.headline: Oman stocks tick lower in active week's trade.

text.p: Shares on the Oman stock exchange ticked down in the week to Wednesday but the volume of trade, led by banks and financial stocks, rose in the first full week's trade since the Eid holiday.
The Muscat Securities Market said the index slipped to 272.73 points from 273.18 the previous week.
The total value of trade rose to 12.12 million rials from 7.47 million the previous week, which was shortened by the Eid holiday. Some 4.14 million shares were traded, up from 2.46 million.
The exchange said banking and financial shares dominated the market, accounting for 67 percent of trade, followed by insurance firms with 17 percent, and services with 15 percent.
Bank Muscat Al Ahli Al Omani was among the week's most active stocks, with 210,000 shares worth 1.09 million rials changing hands. The stock closed lower, at 5.100 rials from 5.180 a week earlier.
Dhofar International Development and Investment Co ended the week at 2.830 rials from 2.760.
Al-Ahlia Portfolio closed at 7.650 rials from 7.450 the previous week.
Of the 69 shares traded in the week, 31 rose, 20 dipped and 18 were unchanged.
